```{python}
#| label: setup

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join('..', '..'))
from chart_utils import use_slide_chart_defaults, figure_with_shift_toggle, CHART_CONFIG
use_slide_chart_defaults()

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join('..', '..', '..', 'run_sets', 'shorten-lengthen-all-work-trips'))
import report_loader as loader

frames = loader.load()
scenario_ids = frames['scenario_ids']
corridor_volumes = frames['corridor_volumes']
freeway_by_county = frames['freeway_by_county']
corridor_orientation = frames['corridor_orientation']
vmt_vhd = frames['vmt_vhd_by_county_facility']
congested_miles = frames['congested_miles']
vht_hh = frames['vht_per_household']
transit = frames['transit_ridership']
trip_length = frames['hbw_trip_length']
trip_length_dist = frames['hbw_trip_length_distribution']

COUNTY_ORDER = ['Salt Lake', 'Davis', 'Utah', 'Weber', 'Box Elder', 'Region']
TRANSIT_LINE_ORDER = ['FrontRunner', 'TRAX Blue Line', 'TRAX Green Line', 'TRAX Red Line', loader.BUS_LABEL]
PERIOD_ORDER = loader.PERIOD_ORDER  # ['Peak', 'Off-Peak', 'Daily']
SHIFT_LABEL_FMT = '{v:+d}%'

# Signed shift levels (-10/-5/+5/+10) don't fit the shared deck-wide toggle
# bar (reports/global_toggle_bar.html) used by the companion run sets' own
# decks -- that bar's shift-level buttons are hardcoded to unsigned
# "5%"/"10%"/"25%" labels (built for bring-work-trips-closer-to-home's
# geography x shift factorial) and are shared across every deck that
# includes it, so it isn't extended here. This deck uses LOCAL per-chart
# toggle buttons instead (figure_with_shift_toggle's default behavior, no
# global_shift/global_period/global_pct) -- self-contained, no shared-file
# changes, and every button label correctly shows its sign.
BAR_COLOR = '#2a78d6'
SHIFT_COLORS = {'-10%': '#b2182b', '-5%': '#ef8a62', '+5%': '#67a9cf', '+10%': '#2166ac'}
SHIFT_LABEL_ORDER = ['-10%', '-5%', '+5%', '+10%']

PRIMARY_SHIFT_PCT = -10

# Two-column slides (::: {.column width="50%"}) need each chart's own
# width override -- see bring-work-trips-closer-to-home/slides.qmd's own
# docstring for why.
HALF_WIDTH = 540
```

## The Question

::: {.incremental}
- What if **every** home-based-work commute shifted a little — shorter or longer — not just the longest ones, and not just in one target area?
- Sketch test: shift every origin's own average HBW trip length by a fixed percentage (-10% / -5% / +5% / +10%), reweighting each origin's *existing* destination pattern
- Applied to 100% of origins with HBW trips, region-wide — not a selected subset
- 2027 RTP adoption-year network, model v10.0.0-beta.1 — same baseline model run as the companion run sets
:::

::: {.notes}
This is a directional, order-of-magnitude check, not a land-use forecast — see the caveats slide. Different mechanism from both companion run sets: Closer targets a named geography; Shorten trims only the longest-distance tail; this one shifts every origin's mean, both directions.
:::

## Big Picture: All Four Shift Levels at Once
```{python}
region_shift = vmt_vhd[
    (vmt_vhd['CO_NAME'] == 'Region') & (vmt_vhd['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO) & (vmt_vhd['period'] == 'Peak')
].groupby(['shift_pct'], as_index=False)[['delta_DY_VMT', 'base_DY_VMT', 'delta_DY_VHD', 'base_DY_VHD']].sum()
region_shift['pct_DY_VMT'] = region_shift['delta_DY_VMT'] / region_shift['base_DY_VMT'] * 100
region_shift['pct_DY_VHD'] = region_shift['delta_DY_VHD'] / region_shift['base_DY_VHD'] * 100
region_shift['shift_label'] = region_shift['shift_pct'].apply(lambda v: f'{int(v):+d}%')

def _big_picture(y_col, y_title, title):
    fig = px.bar(
        region_shift, x='shift_label', y=y_col, color='shift_label',
        category_orders={'shift_label': SHIFT_LABEL_ORDER},
        color_discrete_map=SHIFT_COLORS,
        labels={'shift_label': 'Shift', y_col: y_title},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
    for trace in fig.data:
        if trace.hovertemplate:
            trace.hovertemplate = trace.hovertemplate.replace('%{y}', '%{y:+,.3r}%')
    fig.update_layout(height=420, width=HALF_WIDTH, title=dict(text=title, font_size=14))
    return fig
```

```

```

All four shift levels at once, region-wide, Peak period — the effect roughly mirrors across the 0% line, shorter vs. longer.

## Congestion: VHD by County
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
vhd_df = vmt_vhd.copy()
vhd_df['CO_NAME'] = pd.Categorical(vhd_df['CO_NAME'], categories=COUNTY_ORDER, ordered=True)
vhd_by_county = vhd_df[vhd_df['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO].groupby(
    ['CO_NAME', 'shift_pct', 'period'], as_index=False, observed=True
)[['delta_DY_VHD', 'base_DY_VHD']].sum()
vhd_by_county['pct_DY_VHD'] = vhd_by_county['delta_DY_VHD'] / vhd_by_county['base_DY_VHD'] * 100

def _build_vhd_county(sub, y_col='delta_DY_VHD'):
    fig = px.bar(
        sub, x='CO_NAME', y=y_col, color_discrete_sequence=[BAR_COLOR],
        category_orders={'CO_NAME': COUNTY_ORDER},
        labels={'CO_NAME': 'County', y_col: 'Δ VHD (hrs)'},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(
    vhd_by_county, _build_vhd_county, pct_col='pct_DY_VHD', default_shift=-10, shift_label_fmt=SHIFT_LABEL_FMT,
    value_axis_title='Δ VHD (hrs)', pct_axis_title='Δ VHD (%)',
    period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER,
)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='Change in VHD by County', font_size=15))
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

## Why: Vehicle Miles Traveled
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
vmt_by_county = vhd_df[vhd_df['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO].groupby(
    ['CO_NAME', 'shift_pct', 'period'], as_index=False, observed=True
)[['delta_DY_VMT', 'base_DY_VMT']].sum()
vmt_by_county['pct_DY_VMT'] = vmt_by_county['delta_DY_VMT'] / vmt_by_county['base_DY_VMT'] * 100

def _build_vmt_county(sub, y_col='delta_DY_VMT'):
    fig = px.bar(
        sub, x='CO_NAME', y=y_col, color_discrete_sequence=[BAR_COLOR],
        category_orders={'CO_NAME': COUNTY_ORDER},
        labels={'CO_NAME': 'County', y_col: 'Δ VMT (mi)'},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(
    vmt_by_county, _build_vmt_county, pct_col='pct_DY_VMT', default_shift=-10, shift_label_fmt=SHIFT_LABEL_FMT,
    value_axis_title='Δ VMT (mi)', pct_axis_title='Δ VMT (%)',
    period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER,
)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='Change in VMT by County', font_size=15))
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

::: {.notes}
Shorter commutes mean less driving; longer ones mean more. Less/more driving on congested facilities is why delay moves the same direction.
:::

## Severe Congestion: Miles Over Capacity
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
cm_ft = congested_miles[(congested_miles['CO_NAME'] == 'Region') & (congested_miles['scenario_id'] != loader.BASELINE_SCENARIO)].copy()
cm_base_ft = cm_ft['base_congested_miles']
cm_ft['pct_congested_miles'] = (
    (cm_ft['delta_congested_miles'] / cm_base_ft.where(cm_base_ft > 0, 1) * 100).where(cm_base_ft > 0, 0.0)
)
cm_ft_order = cm_ft[(cm_ft['period'] == 'Peak') & (cm_ft['shift_pct'] == -10)].groupby('FTCLASS')['delta_congested_miles'].sum().sort_values().index.tolist()

def _build_congested_miles(sub, y_col='delta_congested_miles'):
    fig = px.bar(
        sub, x='FTCLASS', y=y_col, color_discrete_sequence=[BAR_COLOR],
        category_orders={'FTCLASS': cm_ft_order},
        labels={'FTCLASS': 'Facility Type', y_col: 'Δ Congested Miles'},
    )
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line_color='#c3c2b7', line_width=1)
    fig.update_layout(xaxis_tickangle=-15)
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(
    cm_ft, _build_congested_miles, pct_col='pct_congested_miles', default_shift=-10, shift_label_fmt=SHIFT_LABEL_FMT,
    value_axis_title='Δ Congested Miles', pct_axis_title='Δ Congested Miles (%)',
    period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER,
)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='Change in Miles of Severe Congestion (V/C &gt; 1.0)', font_size=15))
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

Miles of roadway with volume/capacity > 1.0 — a length-based capacity read, distinct from delay (VHD), more directly comparable to how funding/capacity-expansion needs are scoped.

## Trip Length Distribution
```{python}
#| fig-align: center
td = trip_length_dist.copy()
td['shift_label'] = td['shift_pct'].apply(lambda v: 'Baseline' if v == 0 else f'{int(v):+d}%')

def _build_td(sub):
    fig = px.line(
        sub, x='bin_label', y='share_pct', color='shift_label', markers=True,
        category_orders={'bin_label': loader.DISTANCE_BIN_LABELS, 'shift_label': ['Baseline'] + SHIFT_LABEL_ORDER},
        color_discrete_map={**SHIFT_COLORS, 'Baseline': '#898781'},
        labels={'bin_label': 'HBW Trip Length', 'share_pct': 'Share of Trips (%)', 'shift_label': 'Scenario'},
    )
    fig.update_traces(selector=dict(name='Baseline'), line=dict(color='black', dash='dash', width=2), marker=dict(color='black'))
    return fig

fig = figure_with_shift_toggle(
    td, _build_td, always_include=[0], default_shift=-10, shift_label_fmt=SHIFT_LABEL_FMT,
    period_col='period', default_period='Peak', period_order=PERIOD_ORDER,
)
fig.update_layout(height=460, title=dict(text='HBW Trip Length Distribution, Baseline vs. Shift<br><sup>2-mile bins, Peak/Off-Peak-correct distance</sup>', font_size=15))
fig.update_xaxes(range=[-0.5, loader.DISTANCE_BIN_EDGES.index(30) - 0.5])
fig.update_yaxes(range=[0, 25])
fig.show(config=CHART_CONFIG)
```

The distribution shifts left when shortening, right when lengthening — the mechanism working as intended, region-wide, in both directions.

## Caveats
:::  {.incremental}
- **Not a real land-use/economic forecast** — no businesses relocate, no zoning changes simulated
- **Feasibility not checked** — model doesn't confirm destinations could absorb reweighted trips
- **Sketch-level, order-of-magnitude** — trips manually reweighted on today's existing pattern
- **HBW trips only** — other trip purposes untouched
- **Every origin touched, but not identically** — a small share (no existing trips, or a single destination) can't shift at all
- **Symmetric by construction** — the -X%/+X% pairing is the same algorithm run each direction, not an independent empirical finding
- **Same mechanism at all four levels** — tests sensitivity to size and direction, not to method
:::
